items.title: Live: Jane Hume to run for Liberal deputy as shadow frontbencher quits ahead of challenge
items.description: Tasmanian Liberal frontbencher Claire Chandler has resigned from the shadow ministry, following Angus Taylor as he prepares to challenge for the party leadership. Follow live.

items.title: Taylor's supporters say he has the numbers to topple Ley
items.description: Angus Taylor quit the Liberal front bench yesterday ahead of a leadership spill expected to be called against Sussan Ley today.

items.title: Angus Taylor is making his move — but not on his terms
items.description: Angus Taylor was holidaying in Europe when his colleagues began manoeuvring to topple Sussan Ley. A leadership spill this week wasn't what he or Sussan Ley wanted.

items.title: Bondi 'deeply sorry' over Epstein's crimes but not over handling of files
items.description: US Attorney-General Pam Bondi faces furious questions over the censorship of names in the Epstein files at a hearing punctuated by heated shouting matches.

items.title: James Van Der Beek, star of Dawson's Creek, dies aged 48
items.description: The American actor was best known for his starring role as Dawson Leery in Dawson's Creek from 1998 to 2003.

items.title: Live: Olympic great impressed by Aussies as James and Guseli reach halfpipe final
items.description: Australian Scotty James starts his quest for a third Olympic medal, qualifying in first place with a phenomenal run in snowboard halfpipe qualifying at the Milano Cortina Winter Olympics. Follow live.

items.title: Violent criminals and alleged killers behind alleged CFMEU corruption
items.description: Members of bikie gangs, convicted murderers and violent criminals are among more than 25 people who allegedly benefited from or are linked to corrupt behaviour at the CFMEU, according to a report.

items.title: Live: Australian dollar rises above 71 US cents, ASX to open flat
items.description: Australian stocks are set to open flat after a lacklustre session on Wall Street, with major companies, including Origin Energy, AMP and Temple & Webster, releasing earnings results today. Follow the latest updates in our live blog.

items.title: Canadian school shooter identified as 18-year-old Jesse Van Rootselaar
items.description: The person who carried out a school massacre in a remote Canadian community is an 18-year-old woman with mental health issues, police say.

items.title: PM 'not contemplating failure' as Closing the Gap deadline looms
items.description: Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is bullish on closing the gap between Indigenous and non-Indigenous people ahead of handing down his annual report card on the progress made.

items.title: Australia's frozen ghost town leaves behind a toxic legacy
items.description: The ABC has been given rare access to an abandoned Australian base in Antarctica that continues to pose a threat to the environment.

items.title: A look at Iran's non-negotiable ballistic missile program
items.description: Iran has spent decades building the largest and most diverse ballistic missile stockpile in the Middle East and is refusing US demands to put limits on the weapons program.

items.title: Possible El Niño within months raises potential for hot year across Australia
items.description: The first El Niño in three years could develop during the coming months, raising the possibility of worsening drought and extreme heat across Australia in 2026.

items.title: Sarah's solo hike was meant to be empowering. Then a man stepped onto the trail
items.description: A woman's solo hike through regional Victoria took a disturbing turn near Daylesford, raising questions about safety and police responses.

items.title: Bougainville mine that sparked a civil war on rapid path to reopening
items.description: The Autonomous Bougainville Government signs a secretive deal to reopen a huge gold and copper mine that sparked a catastrophic civil war three decades ago.

items.title: Days before thousands of people crossed a new bridge, a 'large crack' was found
items.description: Days before the official opening, the Tasmanian government's largest-ever infrastructure project hit a hurdle, with a large crack picked up in one of the Bridgewater Bridge's piers detected and fixed, documents show.

items.title: Today's quiz is noice, it's different, it's unusual
items.description: It's an Aussie classic, but do you know who delivered these iconic lines in Kath & Kim? Put down your car-donnay and footy franks and show us what you've got.

items.title: Man charged one year after 'shocking' abuse of puppy captured on camera
items.description: A man has been charged with animal cruelty a year after neighbours first made a complaint to the RSPCA.

items.title: Carers close to 'breaking point' as support services buckle under demand
items.description: An organisation that helps people caring for vulnerable family members in WA is experiencing unprecedented demand, with services unable to keep up with the community's needs.

items.title: How a 'loner' paedophile hid in plain sight in the suburbs of Perth
items.description: "A regular sort of bloke," is how one of Jason Forbes's neighbours described the 39-year-old electrician — but inside the walls of his unassuming Baldivis home, he was hiding a dark secret.

items.title: Darwin traditional owners feel 'bulldozed' by ambitious solar farm company
items.description: A renewable energy company planning to build a solar farm near Darwin is seeking a court ruling that no native title claim exists at the proposed site.

items.title: Fresh video shows police pushing Herzog protester before fight broke out
items.description: A new video filmed by a bystander and shared with ABC NEWS Verify shows the full minute before two police officers began punching a protester, shedding light on the beginning of the altercation.

items.title: US officials say cartel drones behind sudden closure of Texas airport
items.description: US officials say a sudden 10-day ban came into effect around El Paso International Airport after cartel drones from nearby Mexico breached American airspace.

items.title: China's president makes rare acknowledgement of corruption in army
items.description: Xi Jinping's comments were the first public admission of issues in China's armed forces since an investigation was launched into senior members of the body that overseas the country's military.

items.title: Fatberg responsible for foul-smelling debris balls is 'inaccessible' for Sydney Water
items.description: The debris balls that have washed up on NSW beaches in recent years are likely to continue as Sydney Water admits a massive fatberg it cannot reach is clogging sewers.
